schedule.model: checks in one layer must have disjoint physical-bit supports

algorithm: measure the 1620 local and 27 global checks in two conflict-free layers
discard zero-local-syndrome cells; under total error weight <=6 they contain no nonzero local-code error
enumerate the eight local-coset candidates only on affected cells and prune total weight >6
use the 27 global syndrome bits to select the unique remaining candidate

theorem: The [2025,378,14]_2 router code admits an explicit rank-1647 sparse parity-check matrix, an optimal two-layer conflict-free syndrome schedule, and a finite local-coset decoder correcting every pattern of at most six arbitrary physical bit errors.
boundary: Schedule depth is exact only in the disjoint-support check model and is not a measured hardware clock depth; radius 6 is the classical bounded-distance guarantee, not a physical threshold.
